sections.category: Alibaba previews Qwen3.8 at 2.4 trillion parameters and promises an open-weight release, its first multimodal model above the trillion-parameter line

bullets.body: Alibaba's Qwen team said today that Qwen3.8 is launching and will go open-weight, at 2.4 trillion parameters — the first Qwen multimodal model above the trillion-parameter line, taking images, video and documents. Access starts proprietary: Qwen3.8-Max-Preview is live now through Alibaba's Token Plan, Qoder and QoderWork at a tenth of standard pricing, with the open-weight drop promised but undated. Alibaba's claim is that the model sits second only to Claude Fable 5 among generally available systems and should beat Qwen3.7-Max on coding and complex productivity work, but no benchmark results have been published to support either statement. The preview-then-open sequencing is itself the notable part. Alibaba built its reputation shipping top models with weights available at launch, and Qwen3.8 repeats the Qwen3.6-Max pattern of monetizing a preview window first, which means the announcement is a commitment rather than a delivery. Timing puts it three days behind Moonshot's Kimi K3 at 2.8 trillion parameters, and Moonshot is reported at roughly $300 million in annual recurring revenue with an IPO targeted inside six months — so the parameter-count race and the capital-markets race are now running on the same clock. For anyone tracking the open-versus-closed gap, the durable observation is that the two largest announced open-weight models in the world are both Chinese, both above 2 trillion parameters, and both announced inside a single week.

sections.category: A botnet called NadMesh scans the internet for exposed Ollama, ComfyUI and Langflow instances and strips cloud credentials out of them

bullets.body: QiAnXin's XLab published analysis of a botnet it calls NadMesh, which hunts self-hosted AI infrastructure rather than conventional web targets — exposed instances of ComfyUI, Ollama, n8n, Open WebUI, Langflow and Gradio. What it takes once inside is credentials, not compute: cloud keys from environment variables, Kubernetes service-account tokens, the contents of ~/.aws/config, .env and ~/.docker/config.json, plus model access and whatever MCP tools the host can call. The operator's own dashboard, captured July 10, claimed 3,811 unique AWS keys and 47 credential hauls across its last 100 records, while XLab's sensors observed around 139 distinct source IPs per day. Those operator figures deserve skepticism — the same dashboard shows a 17,700 total-deploy counter sitting above a funnel claiming 95,700 in the preceding 24 hours, which cannot both be true. Initial access skews to ordinary misconfiguration rather than anything AI-specific: Docker API remote code execution at 30.31% of observed traffic, Jenkins script-console execution at 22.28%, weak telnet passwords at 10.36%, Redis at 8.29%. The recommended response is blunt — get ports 8188, 11434, 7860 and 5678 behind authentication or off the public internet, and rotate anything that was reachable. The structural shift is that the local-inference stack has become a credential-theft target in its own right. The defaults that made these tools pleasant to run, binding broadly and skipping auth and leaving keys in the environment, are now an enumerated attack surface, and a workstation running Ollama next to a cloud credential file is a lateral-movement path rather than a hobby setup.

citations.label: The Hacker News - New NadMesh botnet hunts exposed AI services for cloud keys and Kubernetes tokens

sections.category: Moonshine Micro fits voice detection, speech recognition and neural text-to-speech into 470KB of RAM on an 80-cent microcontroller

bullets.body: Moonshine AI published Moonshine Micro, an MIT-licensed voice stack that runs the entire loop — voice-activity detection, speech recognition and neural text-to-speech — on a microcontroller, with the Raspberry Pi RP2350 as reference platform at a retail price near 80 cents. The memory budget is the substance of the claim: detection takes about 89 KiB of flash and 36 KiB of SRAM, the SpellingCNN recognizer about 1.3 MiB of flash and 346 KiB of SRAM, and a neural diphone voice pack about 1.8 MiB and 340 KiB, with the assembled demo landing near 3.6 MiB of flash and roughly 468 KiB of SRAM by sharing memory between pipeline stages so the total fits inside the RP2350's 520 KiB. It recognizes about 50 custom words or phrases, retrainable to an application's own vocabulary, and turns speech in to speech out in roughly 0.7 to 1.0 seconds on TensorFlow Lite Micro. The reference demo walks a user through configuring a wifi connection entirely by voice, which is the argument in miniature — no cloud round trip, no API key, no account. This sits at the opposite end of the local-model spectrum from compressing frontier capability onto a workstation: instead of shrinking a large model until it fits, it asks what the smallest genuinely useful language interface is, and answers with a bill of materials cheap enough for disposable hardware. It reached the top of Hacker News on July 18, and the likely reason is that it removes two assumptions at once — voice interfaces have been taken to require either a phone-class system-on-chip or a network connection, and this needs neither.

sections.category: A single researcher's ten-page prompt gets GPT-5.6 to close an oracle-complexity gap in derivative-free convex optimization that had stood since 1996

bullets.body: Phillip Kerger posted a proof on July 14 establishing that minimizing a convex Lipschitz function over a d-dimensional Euclidean ball, deterministically and using only exact function values, requires Omega(d^2 / log(d+1)) queries at accuracy Theta(d^-1/2). That closes, up to polylogarithmic factors, a gap open since 1996 between the known Omega(d) lower bound and Protasov's O(d^2 log^2 d) value-only method; the same machinery extends to mixed-integer instances at roughly d^2 times 2^n queries for d continuous and n discrete variables. The provenance surfaced on July 18, when Kerger described the process publicly: roughly a year of his own work on the problem, unsuccessful attempts with GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5, and then a prompt running about ten pages that laid out the reasonable approaches from the literature — after which GPT-5.6 produced the argument and generated the Lean formalization alongside it. His own framing was that he gave an AI contractor architectural direction rather than a solution, and commenters were quick to observe that the year of failed attempts is precisely what made a ten-page prompt possible. Set against OpenAI's Cycle Double Cover announcement, which ran 64 parallel agents and remains unformalized and un-peer-reviewed, this is the more load-bearing data point because it is smaller: one model instance, one named human author carrying responsibility for the claim, and a machine-checkable artifact at the end of it. The variable that determines whether results like this compound is verification, not agent count.

citations.label: arXiv:2607.13335 - Closing the Oracle-Complexity Gap in Derivative-Free Convex Optimization

sections.category: DeepSeek lines up a second raise in two months at a $74 billion valuation while opening deliberations on a Shanghai STAR Market listing

bullets.body: DeepSeek is preparing a fundraise at roughly 500 billion yuan, about $74 billion, seeking as much as 50 billion yuan — a step up arriving only weeks after a June round that took in about $7.4 billion at a post-money valuation near 450 billion yuan. Alongside it the company has begun early deliberations on listing on Shanghai's STAR Market, with an internal target of completing an IPO filing this year; terms and timetable are both described as unsettled, and a US listing is treated as impractical given Congressional scrutiny of Chinese AI firms. The June round's shareholder register is the part worth holding onto: founder Liang Wenfeng committed 20 billion yuan personally, Tencent put in 10 billion and battery maker CATL 5 billion to become the largest external holders, while China's state AI investment fund holds the only outside board voting rights. What makes this a threshold rather than a headline is what it replaces. DeepSeek ran for years on Liang's quantitative fund High-Flyer, and that self-funding is exactly what let it ship cheap open-weight models without answering to outside capital or a quarterly clock. Two raises inside two months plus a filing target means compute, data-centre capacity and talent costs have outrun what a hedge fund balance sheet can absorb — the lab that made its name proving frontier work could be done cheaply is now financing it the same way everybody else does.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: the AGI Summit closes today, WAIC closes tomorrow, and AMD Advancing AI has sold out its in-person capacity three days before it opens

bullets.body: The nearest item is today. The AGI Summit is on its closing day, July 19, 9 AM to 5 PM at the Palace of Fine Arts, 3301 Lyon Street in San Francisco, with speakers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Stanford, Berkeley and MIT; walk-up tickets started at $199, with a $49 student rate on a valid .edu address. WAIC 2026 in Shanghai closes tomorrow, July 20. After that the calendar's first hard stop is AMD's Advancing AI at Moscone West on July 22-23, and the planning fact there has changed since last week: in-person registration is now full, so the route in is Lisa Su's keynote at 9:30 AM PT on July 23, livestreamed on AMD's YouTube channel, with more than 100 breakouts, tech talks and workshops around it for those who already hold a badge. On the chip and hardware track, July 31 is the date to put on the calendar — 11:59 PM PDT that Friday is the cutoff for the Hot Chips early-registration rate, with cancellations accepted until August 19. Hot Chips itself opens August 23 at Stanford with tutorials on HBM evolution under AI data demand and on RISC-V standards and automotive adoption, drawing Samsung, SK Hynix, NVIDIA and Infineon, and runs through August 25. Further out on the same track, the AI Infra Summit takes the Santa Clara Convention Center September 15-17 with roughly 8,000 attendees and 400-plus speakers across compute, AI data centres, data movement and physical AI; full access is $1,497, and complimentary passes are offered to enterprise technologists in banking, pharma, retail, manufacturing and automotive as well as to hyperscaler technical staff. NVIDIA's GTC does not return to San Jose until March 15-18, 2027. The AI-security track clusters in early August and has firmer shape than it did a week ago. Black Hat USA runs August 1-6 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas — Trainings August 1-4, Briefings August 5-6 — with its dedicated AI Summit on August 4. DEF CON 34 follows August 6-9, and its AI Village is running demos, capture-the-flag and a new poster track on adversarial attacks against agents and agentic systems. SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit takes the Ritz-Carlton at Half Moon Bay on August 11-12. Two later additions are worth booking now rather than in the autumn scramble: SANS runs an AI Cybersecurity Summit on November 2-3 at the Hilton Arlington Rosslyn, $525 in person with live-online attendance free, a hotel-rate deadline of October 9 and refunds until October 14; and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues with London on October 8 and New York on October 21. OWASP Global AppSec USA lands in San Francisco November 5-6. On the developer and infrastructure side: Ai4 in Las Vegas August 4-6; the AI Tinkerers San Francisco meetup on August 9, 6 to 9 PM at Founders Inc, RSVP-gated with limited space; Ray Summit at the San Francisco Marriott Marquis August 24-26; the ACM AI Leadership Summit in Atlanta August 30 through September 2; OpenAI DevDay at Fort Mason September 29; The AI Conference at Pier 48 September 29 through October 1; the Runway AI Summit September 30; World Summit AI in Amsterdam October 7-8; PyTorch Conference in San Jose October 20-21; GitHub Universe October 28-29; AWS re:Invent November 30 through December 4; NeurIPS in December; IEEE-RAS Humanoids in Santa Clara December 7-9; and The AI Summit New York December 9-10. Practical sequencing for the next fortnight: today is the AGI Summit's last chance, Thursday's Advancing AI keynote is now a browser tab rather than a trip across town, and the Hot Chips early rate has to be locked by July 31 — before the early-August Las Vegas security block absorbs both the calendar and the budget.
